questions.subtopic: Screen Test - Business vs Asset Acquisition
questions.stem:
Bayard Corp pays $60,000,000 cash to acquire all of the equity interests in Harbor LLC. Harbor holds no cash or deferred tax balances. The acquisition-date fair values of Harbor's assets are:
Office building | $52,000,000
Land under the office building | $5,600,000
In-place lease intangible for the building's tenants | $1,200,000
Building maintenance service contract intangible | $1,200,000
Bayard applies the screen test in ASC 805-10-55-5A, under which the land, the building, and the in-place lease intangible are treated as a single identifiable asset. What is the concentration of fair value in a single identifiable asset, and what does the screen test indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 86.7%; the transaction is accounted for as a business combination

choices.label: B
choices.text: 98.0%; the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition

choices.label: C
choices.text: 98.0%; the transaction is accounted for as a business combination

choices.label: D
choices.text: 96.0%; the transaction is accounted for as an asset acquisition

questions.explanation: The gross assets acquired total $60,000,000 ($52,000,000 + $5,600,000 + $1,200,000 + $1,200,000), excluding cash and deferred taxes. Because the land, building, and in-place lease intangible are treated as a single identifiable asset, that group has a fair value of $58,800,000, or 98.0% of the gross assets acquired. Substantially all of the fair value is concentrated in a single identifiable asset, so the screen test is met and the set is not a business; Bayard accounts for an asset acquisition, capitalizing transaction costs and recognizing no goodwill. The 86.7% figure counts only the $52,000,000 building and ignores the requirement to combine the land and the in-place lease with it. The 96.0% figure combines only the land and building ($57,600,000) and improperly excludes the in-place lease intangible. Concluding that the transaction is a business combination contradicts the screen test result, which ends the analysis once substantially all of the fair value is concentrated in one asset.
questions.explanationJa: 取得した総資産は現金と繰延税金を除いて $60,000,000（$52,000,000 + $5,600,000 + $1,200,000 + $1,200,000）。土地・建物・インプレースリース無形資産は単一の識別可能資産として扱われるため、そのグループの公正価値は $58,800,000 で総資産の 98.0% を占める。実質的にすべての公正価値が単一資産に集中しているためスクリーンテストに該当し、事業ではない。したがって資産の取得として処理し、取引コストは資産原価に算入、のれんは認識しない。86.7% は建物 $52,000,000 だけを数え、土地とインプレースリースを合算する要件を無視した数値。96.0% は土地と建物 $57,600,000 のみを合算し、インプレースリース無形資産を除外した誤り。集中が認められた時点で分析は終了するため、企業結合と結論づけるのは誤り。

questions.subtopic: Substantive Process Test - Set Without Outputs
questions.stem: Calder Pharma acquires all of the equity of Vantis Labs, an early-stage biotechnology company. Vantis has never generated revenue. The acquired set consists of one in-process research and development project in Phase II clinical trials, specialized laboratory equipment, and an organized workforce of 40 research scientists and technicians with the skills and experience necessary to advance the project through clinical development. The screen test in ASC 805-10-55-5A is not met. Does the acquired set meet the definition of a business?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No. A set that does not produce outputs can never meet the definition of a business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. Because the acquired set generates no revenue, Calder accounts for an asset acquisition and charges the in-process research and development project to expense immediately.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes. The organized research workforce is a substantive process, and the in-process research and development project is an input that the workforce could develop into an output.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes. Any acquisition of a legal entity in which the consideration transferred exceeds the fair value of the identifiable assets is a business combination, because only a business can generate goodwill.

questions.explanation: ASC 805-10-55-5D provides a separate framework for a set that has no outputs. Such a set is a business if it includes both an input and a substantive process, which is satisfied when the set includes an organized workforce with the necessary skills, knowledge, or experience to perform a process that is critical to the ability to develop an input into an output. The 40 research scientists and technicians are that organized workforce, and the Phase II project is an input they can develop. The set is a business, so Calder applies the acquisition method, expenses acquisition-related costs, and capitalizes the in-process research and development as an indefinite-lived intangible until the project is completed or abandoned. The view that a set without outputs can never be a business ignores the no-outputs framework. Charging the in-process project to expense is the treatment required in an asset acquisition when the project has no alternative future use, which is not the conclusion here. Excess consideration over identifiable asset fair values does not by itself establish that a set is a business; in an asset acquisition, any such excess is allocated to the nonfinancial assets acquired rather than recognized as goodwill.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 805-10-55-5D はアウトプットを持たないセットに別枠の判定基準を置く。インプットと実質的なプロセスの両方を含めば事業に該当し、インプットをアウトプットへ発展させるうえで不可欠なプロセスを遂行できる技能・知識・経験を備えた組織化された労働力があれば、この要件を満たす。研究者・技術者40名がその組織化された労働力であり、フェーズII のプロジェクトが彼らの発展させ得るインプットである。よって事業に該当し、取得法を適用して取得関連費用は費用処理し、仕掛研究開発は完了または放棄まで耐用年数不確定の無形資産として資産計上する。アウトプットがなければ事業になり得ないという見方はこの枠組みを無視している。仕掛研究開発の即時費用処理は、代替用途がない場合の資産取得での処理であり本件の結論ではない。対価が識別可能資産の公正価値を上回ることだけでは事業とは判定されない。資産取得ではその超過額はのれんではなく非金融資産へ配分される。

questions.subtopic: Asset Acquisition - Transaction Costs Capitalized
questions.stem: Ridley Corp pays $9,600,000 cash to acquire a group of assets that does not constitute a business, and incurs $400,000 of legal and due diligence fees directly attributable to the transaction. The acquisition-date fair values of the assets acquired are land $3,000,000, building $6,000,000, and equipment $3,000,000. No liabilities are assumed. What amount should Ridley record for the building?
questions.explanation: In an asset acquisition, transaction costs that are directly attributable to the acquisition are capitalized as part of the cost of the assets, unlike a business combination where such costs are expensed. Total cost to allocate is $10,000,000 ($9,600,000 + $400,000). The building's relative fair value is $6,000,000 of the $12,000,000 total, or 50%, so $5,000,000 is allocated to the building. The $4,800,000 amount allocates only the $9,600,000 cash and improperly expenses the transaction costs. The $6,000,000 amount records the building at its stand-alone fair value, which is not permitted when total cost differs from the sum of the fair values. The $5,200,000 amount allocates the cash on a relative fair value basis but then charges the entire $400,000 of transaction costs to the building alone rather than spreading it across all assets acquired.
questions.explanationJa: 資産の取得では、取得に直接起因する取引コストは資産の取得原価に算入する。企業結合で費用処理されるのとは対照的である。配分対象の総原価は $10,000,000（$9,600,000 + $400,000）。建物の相対的公正価値は $12,000,000 のうち $6,000,000 で 50% なので、建物への配分額は $5,000,000。$4,800,000 は現金 $9,600,000 のみを配分し、取引コストを誤って費用処理した金額。$6,000,000 は建物を単独の公正価値で計上した金額で、総原価が公正価値合計と異なる場合には認められない。$5,200,000 は現金を相対的公正価値で配分したうえで、取引コスト $400,000 を全資産に按分せず建物だけに賦課した誤り。

questions.subtopic: Asset Acquisition - Excess Consideration Over Fair Value
questions.stem: Stelling Corp pays $14,000,000 cash to acquire a group of assets that does not constitute a business. The acquisition-date fair values are marketable equity securities $2,000,000, manufacturing equipment $6,000,000, and a patent $4,000,000. No liabilities are assumed and no transaction costs are incurred. What amount should Stelling record for the patent?
questions.explanation: In an asset acquisition, goodwill is never recognized. When the cost exceeds the sum of the fair values of the assets acquired, the excess is allocated to the nonfinancial assets on a relative fair value basis; financial assets such as marketable securities are recorded at their own fair value and receive none of the excess. The securities are recorded at $2,000,000, leaving $12,000,000 of cost for the nonfinancial assets whose combined fair value is $10,000,000. The $2,000,000 excess is allocated $800,000 to the patent ($4,000,000 / $10,000,000), producing $4,800,000. The $4,000,000 amount records the patent at fair value and leaves $2,000,000 unallocated, which would have to become goodwill and is prohibited in an asset acquisition. The $4,666,667 amount spreads the excess over all three assets, including the marketable securities. The $6,000,000 amount charges the entire $2,000,000 excess to the patent instead of spreading it across the equipment and the patent.
questions.explanationJa: 資産の取得ではのれんを一切認識しない。取得原価が取得資産の公正価値合計を上回る場合、超過額は非金融資産へ相対的公正価値で配分する。市場性のある有価証券などの金融資産は自身の公正価値で計上し、超過額の配分を受けない。有価証券は $2,000,000 で計上し、残る $12,000,000 が公正価値合計 $10,000,000 の非金融資産に配分される。超過額 $2,000,000 のうち特許には $4,000,000 / $10,000,000 に相当する $800,000 が配分され、計上額は $4,800,000。$4,000,000 は特許を公正価値のまま計上し $2,000,000 が未配分となるが、これはのれんとなり資産取得では認められない。$4,666,667 は有価証券を含む3資産すべてに超過額を按分した誤り。$6,000,000 は超過額 $2,000,000 の全額を特許のみに賦課し、設備への配分を怠った誤り。

questions.subtopic: Consideration Transferred - Assets Remaining in Combined Entity
questions.stem: Corbin Corp acquires 100% of the outstanding shares of Devon Inc, which will continue to operate as Corbin's wholly owned subsidiary. As part of the arrangement, Corbin transfers a manufacturing facility with a carrying amount of $3,000,000 and an acquisition-date fair value of $4,200,000 to Devon Inc itself. The facility will be used by Devon after the combination and therefore remains within the combined entity. How should Corbin account for the transferred facility on the acquisition date?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Measure the facility at its $4,200,000 fair value and recognize a $1,200,000 gain in earnings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Measure the facility at its $3,000,000 carrying amount and recognize no gain or loss, because the facility remains within the combined entity and Corbin retains control of it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Measure the facility at its $4,200,000 fair value and credit the $1,200,000 excess to additional paid-in capital.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Measure the facility at its $3,000,000 carrying amount and increase goodwill by the $1,200,000 of unrecognized appreciation.

questions.explanation: Consideration transferred is generally measured at acquisition-date fair value, and the acquirer recognizes a gain or loss on nonmonetary assets transferred as consideration. That rule applies only when the transferred assets leave the combined entity, which happens when they are transferred to the former owners of the acquiree. Here the facility is transferred to the acquiree, which Corbin controls after the combination, so the facility remains within the combined entity. ASC 805-30-30-8 requires the acquirer to measure those assets at their carrying amount immediately before the acquisition date, so the facility stays at $3,000,000 and no gain or loss is recognized. Recognizing a $1,200,000 gain would apply the treatment reserved for assets transferred to the former owners. Crediting the appreciation to additional paid-in capital has no support, because the transfer is not an equity issuance. Increasing goodwill by the unrecognized appreciation would double count value that the acquirer still controls.
questions.explanationJa: 移転した対価は原則として取得日の公正価値で測定し、対価として引き渡した非貨幣性資産については取得企業が損益を認識する。ただしこの取扱いは、資産が結合後の企業の外へ出る場合、すなわち被取得企業の旧所有者へ引き渡される場合に限られる。本件では施設は被取得企業そのものへ移転され、結合後も Corbin が支配するため、施設は結合後企業の内部に留まる。ASC 805-30-30-8 はこの場合、取得日直前の帳簿価額で測定し損益を認識しないことを求めるため、施設は $3,000,000 のまま計上される。$1,200,000 の利得認識は旧所有者へ引き渡した場合の処理を誤って当てはめたもの。含み益を資本剰余金へ貸記する処理は、株式の発行ではないため根拠がない。含み益分だけのれんを増やす処理は、取得企業が引き続き支配する価値を二重計上することになる。

questions.subtopic: Acquisition-Related Costs vs Issuance Costs
questions.stem:
Vantage Corp acquired 100% of Larkin Inc on June 1, Year 1 in a business combination. Vantage funded the cash portion of the purchase price by issuing bonds and also issued its own common shares directly to Larkin's former shareholders. Vantage incurred the following costs in connection with the transaction:
Legal and due diligence fees | $700,000
Finder's fee paid to an investment bank | $250,000
Costs to register and issue the common shares given as consideration | $180,000
Underwriting and issuance costs on the bonds issued to fund the cash portion | $220,000
Salaries of Vantage's internal acquisitions department allocated to the transaction | $150,000
What total amount should Vantage charge to expense in the period the costs are incurred?
questions.explanation: Under ASC 805-10-25-23 acquisition-related costs are expensed as incurred and are not part of consideration transferred, and that includes internal general and administrative costs allocated to the deal. The legal and due diligence fees of $700,000, the finder's fee of $250,000, and the allocated internal salaries of $150,000 total $1,100,000 of expense. The $180,000 of share registration and issuance costs are a reduction of additional paid-in capital, not an expense. The $220,000 of bond issuance costs are presented as a direct deduction from the carrying amount of the debt and amortized to interest expense over the term of the bonds, so only a small portion affects earnings in the current period. The $950,000 amount improperly excludes the allocated internal salaries. The $1,320,000 amount improperly expenses the bond issuance costs immediately. The $1,500,000 amount expenses every cost listed, including the equity and debt issuance costs that are charged to equity and to the debt carrying amount.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 805-10-25-23 により取得関連費用は発生時に費用処理し、移転対価には含めない。案件に配賦された社内の一般管理費もこれに含まれる。法務・デューデリジェンス費用 $700,000、仲介手数料 $250,000、配賦された社内人件費 $150,000 の合計 $1,100,000 が費用となる。株式の登録・発行費用 $180,000 は費用ではなく資本剰余金の減額。社債の発行費用 $220,000 は負債の帳簿価額から直接控除し、償還期間にわたり支払利息として償却するため、当期の損益に影響するのは一部にとどまる。$950,000 は配賦された社内人件費を誤って除外した金額。$1,320,000 は社債発行費用を即時費用処理した誤り。$1,500,000 は資本や負債の帳簿価額に賦課すべき発行費用まで含め、列挙されたすべてを費用処理した誤り。

questions.subtopic: Consideration Transferred - Shares Measured at Acquisition Date
questions.stem: On March 1, Year 1, Halstead Corp and Marrow Inc signed a merger agreement under which Halstead would issue 0.5 shares of its $1 par common stock for each of Marrow's 400,000 outstanding common shares and pay $1,800,000 cash. The combination closed and Halstead obtained control on June 30, Year 1. The market price of Halstead's common stock was $46 per share on March 1, $52 per share on June 30, and $55 per share on July 31. What amount should Halstead record as consideration transferred?
questions.explanation: Equity interests issued as consideration are measured at fair value on the acquisition date, which is the date the acquirer obtains control, not the date the agreement was announced or signed. Halstead issues 200,000 shares (400,000 x 0.5) valued at the June 30 price of $52, or $10,400,000, plus $1,800,000 cash, for total consideration transferred of $12,200,000. Par value is irrelevant to measurement and affects only the split between common stock and additional paid-in capital. The $10,400,000 amount omits the cash paid. The $11,000,000 amount uses the March 1 announcement price of $46. The $12,800,000 amount uses the July 31 price of $55, which is after control was obtained.
questions.explanationJa: 対価として発行する持分は、取得日すなわち支配を獲得した日の公正価値で測定する。公表日や契約調印日ではない。Halstead は 400,000 × 0.5 = 200,000 株を発行し、6月30日の株価 $52 で $10,400,000。これに現金 $1,800,000 を加えた $12,200,000 が移転対価となる。額面は測定に無関係で、資本金と資本剰余金の内訳に影響するだけである。$10,400,000 は現金を含め忘れた金額。$11,000,000 は3月1日の公表時株価 $46 を用いた誤り。$12,800,000 は支配獲得後である7月31日の株価 $55 を用いた誤り。

questions.subtopic: Step Acquisition - Remeasurement and Reclassified OCI
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 3, Keswick Corp held a 30% equity method investment in Alden Inc with a carrying amount of $2,400,000. Keswick's stockholders' equity included $180,000 of accumulated other comprehensive income representing Keswick's share of Alden's cumulative foreign currency translation adjustments. On that date, Keswick paid $6,300,000 cash for Alden's remaining 70% and obtained control. The fair value of the previously held 30% interest on January 1, Year 3 was $2,700,000. What total amount should Keswick recognize in Year 3 net income as a result of obtaining control of Alden?
questions.explanation: In a business combination achieved in stages, the acquirer remeasures its previously held equity interest to acquisition-date fair value and recognizes the resulting gain or loss in earnings. The remeasurement gain is $300,000 ($2,700,000 fair value less the $2,400,000 carrying amount). ASC 805-10-25-10 further requires amounts previously recognized in other comprehensive income related to the previously held interest to be reclassified into earnings on the same basis that would apply if the interest had been disposed of, so the $180,000 of cumulative translation adjustment is also recognized in income. Total income effect is $480,000. The $300,000 amount stops at the remeasurement gain and leaves the translation adjustment stranded in equity. The $120,000 amount subtracts the translation adjustment instead of adding it. Recognizing nothing would treat the step acquisition as an equity transaction, which applies only to changes in ownership that do not result in a change of control.
questions.explanationJa: 段階取得による企業結合では、取得企業は従前保有持分を取得日の公正価値で再測定し、生じた損益を当期損益に認識する。再測定益は公正価値 $2,700,000 − 帳簿価額 $2,400,000 = $300,000。さらに ASC 805-10-25-10 は、従前保有持分に関してその他の包括利益に計上されていた金額を、当該持分を処分した場合と同じ基礎で損益へ組み替えることを求めるため、累積換算調整額 $180,000 も損益に認識する。合計の損益影響は $480,000。$300,000 は再測定益だけで止め、換算調整額を資本に残したままにした金額。$120,000 は換算調整額を加算すべきところを減算した誤り。ゼロとする処理は段階取得を資本取引として扱うもので、支配の変動を伴わない持分変動にのみ当てはまる。

questions.subtopic: Contingent Consideration - Liability vs Equity Classification
questions.stem: Orion Corp completes a business combination on January 1, Year 1 and agrees to one of the arrangements below with the former owners of the acquiree. Which arrangement should Orion classify as a liability at the acquisition date?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An obligation to issue 60,000 additional Orion common shares if the acquiree's cumulative revenue for Years 1 through 3 exceeds $40,000,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An obligation to issue however many Orion common shares are needed to deliver $6,000,000 of value if the acquiree's cumulative revenue for Years 1 through 3 exceeds $40,000,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An obligation to issue 60,000 additional Orion common shares to the former owners only if they remain employed by the acquiree through the end of Year 3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A right to have 10,000 of the Orion shares already issued to the former owners returned to Orion if cumulative revenue for Years 1 through 3 falls below $40,000,000.

questions.explanation: Contingent consideration is classified as a liability or as equity by applying ASC 480 and ASC 815-40. An obligation to deliver a variable number of the acquirer's own shares whose aggregate value is fixed at $6,000,000 exposes the holder to no equity price risk and is a liability under ASC 480-10-25-14, remeasured at fair value through earnings each period. An obligation to issue a fixed number of 60,000 shares settles in a fixed number of the acquirer's own equity instruments and is classified in equity, so it is not remeasured. An arrangement that requires the former owners to remain employed is not contingent consideration at all; it is post-combination compensation expense recognized over the service period. A right to have a fixed number of previously issued shares returned is settled in the acquirer's own equity instruments and is therefore also classified within equity.
questions.explanationJa: 条件付対価の負債・資本の分類は ASC 480 および ASC 815-40 を適用して判定する。総額 $6,000,000 という固定金額を引き渡すために変動する株数を発行する義務は、相手方が株価変動リスクを負わないため ASC 480-10-25-14 により負債となり、毎期公正価値で再測定して差額を損益に計上する。60,000 株という固定株数を発行する義務は、取得企業自身の持分金融商品の固定数で決済されるため資本分類となり再測定しない。旧所有者の継続勤務を条件とする取決めはそもそも条件付対価ではなく、勤務期間にわたり結合後の報酬費用として認識する。既発行株式の固定株数を返還させる権利も取得企業自身の持分金融商品で決済されるため資本の区分に分類される。

questions.subtopic: Equity-Classified Contingent Consideration - No Remeasurement
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Orbit Corp acquired 100% of Palmer Inc for $8,000,000 cash plus an agreement to issue 100,000 shares of Orbit common stock on December 31, Year 2 if Palmer's cumulative operating income exceeds a specified target. The acquisition-date fair value of the contingent share arrangement was $1,400,000, and the arrangement is appropriately classified in equity. The acquisition-date fair value of Palmer's identifiable net assets was $8,600,000. The target was met, and on December 31, Year 2 Orbit issued the 100,000 shares, which had a fair value of $2,100,000 on that date. What amounts should Orbit report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Goodwill of $800,000 and a $700,000 loss in Year 2 earnings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Goodwill of $1,500,000 and no amount in earnings in any period

choices.label: C
choices.text: Goodwill of $800,000 and no amount in earnings in any period

choices.label: D
choices.text: No goodwill and a $600,000 bargain purchase gain at the acquisition date

questions.explanation: Consideration transferred includes the acquisition-date fair value of contingent consideration, so it is $9,400,000 ($8,000,000 cash plus $1,400,000), and goodwill is $800,000 ($9,400,000 less the $8,600,000 of identifiable net assets). Contingent consideration classified in equity is not remeasured after the acquisition date under ASC 805-30-35-1, and its subsequent settlement is accounted for within equity. The increase in the shares' value to $2,100,000 therefore has no effect on earnings and no effect on goodwill; the settlement simply reclassifies $1,400,000 from the contingent consideration equity account to common stock and additional paid-in capital. Recognizing a $700,000 loss applies liability classification treatment to an equity-classified arrangement. Goodwill of $1,500,000 measures the contingent consideration at its settlement-date value of $2,100,000 rather than its acquisition-date fair value. Treating the transaction as a $600,000 bargain purchase omits the contingent consideration from consideration transferred entirely.
questions.explanationJa: 移転対価には条件付対価の取得日公正価値が含まれるため $8,000,000 + $1,400,000 = $9,400,000 となり、のれんは $9,400,000 − 識別可能純資産 $8,600,000 = $800,000。資本に分類された条件付対価は ASC 805-30-35-1 により取得日後に再測定せず、決済も資本の中で処理する。株式価値が $2,100,000 へ上昇しても損益にものれんにも影響せず、決済時は条件付対価の資本勘定 $1,400,000 を資本金と資本剰余金へ振り替えるだけである。$700,000 の損失認識は資本分類の取決めに負債分類の処理を当てはめた誤り。のれん $1,500,000 は条件付対価を取得日公正価値ではなく決済日の $2,100,000 で測定した誤り。$600,000 の負ののれんとする処理は、条件付対価を移転対価から完全に除外した誤り。

questions.subtopic: Contingent Consideration - Measurement Period vs Subsequent Change
questions.stem: Lodestar Corp acquired Fairfield Inc on April 1, Year 1 and recognized a liability-classified contingent consideration obligation at a provisional acquisition-date fair value of $1,500,000, based on management's preliminary estimate of Fairfield's probability of winning a government contract. In November Year 1, and within the measurement period, Lodestar received a valuation report showing that the April 1, Year 1 fair value of the obligation was actually $1,900,000 because of information about the bidding process that existed at the acquisition date but was unknown to Lodestar at that time. Separately, Fairfield won the contract in December Year 1, which increased the fair value of the obligation to $2,600,000 at December 31, Year 1. What is the effect on goodwill and Year 1 earnings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Goodwill increases $1,100,000, with no effect on Year 1 earnings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Goodwill is unchanged, and Year 1 earnings include a $1,100,000 loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: Goodwill increases $400,000, with no effect on Year 1 earnings, because all changes in the fair value of contingent consideration are adjusted against goodwill

choices.label: D
choices.text: Goodwill increases $400,000, and Year 1 earnings include a $700,000 loss

questions.explanation: The two changes have different causes and different accounting. The $400,000 increase from $1,500,000 to $1,900,000 results from new information about facts and circumstances that existed at the acquisition date, so it is a measurement period adjustment that increases the contingent consideration liability and increases goodwill by $400,000. The further increase from $1,900,000 to $2,600,000 results from Fairfield winning the contract after the acquisition date, which is a post-acquisition event, so the $700,000 change in the fair value of a liability-classified obligation is recognized in earnings. Treating the entire $1,100,000 as a goodwill adjustment ignores that the contract win occurred after the acquisition date. Treating the entire $1,100,000 as a loss ignores the qualifying measurement period adjustment. Adjusting only goodwill on the theory that all contingent consideration fair value changes go to goodwill reflects superseded guidance; only measurement period adjustments affect goodwill.
questions.explanationJa: 2つの変動は原因が異なり会計処理も異なる。$1,500,000 から $1,900,000 への $400,000 の増加は、取得日に存在していた事実・状況に関する新情報によるものなので測定期間の修正に該当し、条件付対価負債を増額するとともにのれんを $400,000 増加させる。$1,900,000 から $2,600,000 へのさらなる増加は、取得日後に Fairfield が契約を獲得したという事後の事象によるため、負債分類の条件付対価の公正価値変動 $700,000 として当期損益に認識する。$1,100,000 全額をのれん修正とする処理は、契約獲得が取得日後の事象である点を無視している。$1,100,000 全額を損失とする処理は、適格な測定期間の修正を無視している。条件付対価の公正価値変動をすべてのれんで調整するという考え方は旧基準のもので、のれんに影響するのは測定期間の修正だけである。

questions.subtopic: Contingent Consideration - Acquisition-Date Fair Value Measurement
questions.stem: On July 1, Year 1, Nystrom Corp acquired 100% of Boyle Inc for $12,000,000 cash plus an earnout under which Nystrom will pay an additional $3,000,000 in cash on June 30, Year 3 if Boyle's cumulative EBITDA for the two-year period exceeds $20,000,000, and nothing otherwise. At the acquisition date, Nystrom assessed the probability that the target would be met at 60%, and the present value factor for two years at the appropriate discount rate was 0.90. The acquisition-date fair value of Boyle's identifiable net assets was $13,400,000. What amount of goodwill should Nystrom recognize?

choices.label: D
choices.text: No goodwill; a bargain purchase gain of $1,400,000

questions.explanation: Contingent consideration is included in consideration transferred at its acquisition-date fair value, measured on a probability-weighted and discounted basis. The earnout's fair value is $1,620,000 ($3,000,000 x 60% x 0.90). Consideration transferred is $13,620,000 ($12,000,000 cash plus $1,620,000), and goodwill is $220,000 ($13,620,000 less the $13,400,000 of identifiable net assets). The $400,000 amount uses the undiscounted probability-weighted estimate of $1,800,000 and omits the time value of money. The $1,600,000 amount includes the full undiscounted $3,000,000 maximum payout and ignores both probability weighting and discounting. Concluding that there is a $1,400,000 bargain purchase gain omits the contingent consideration from the measurement of consideration transferred entirely.
questions.explanationJa: 条件付対価は取得日の公正価値で移転対価に含め、確率加重と割引を反映して測定する。アーンアウトの公正価値は $3,000,000 × 60% × 0.90 = $1,620,000。移転対価は $12,000,000 + $1,620,000 = $13,620,000 となり、のれんは $13,620,000 − 識別可能純資産 $13,400,000 = $220,000。$400,000 は割引前の確率加重額 $1,800,000 を用い貨幣の時間価値を無視した金額。$1,600,000 は最大支払額 $3,000,000 をそのまま含め、確率加重も割引も反映していない金額。$1,400,000 の負ののれんとする結論は、条件付対価を移転対価の測定から完全に除外した誤り。

questions.subtopic: Contingent Consideration - Settlement of Liability
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Trawler Corp acquired Denmore Inc and recognized a liability-classified contingent consideration obligation at an acquisition-date fair value of $900,000. The fair value of the obligation was $1,250,000 at December 31, Year 1. On September 30, Year 2, Trawler settled the obligation by paying $1,600,000 cash. No measurement period adjustments were identified. What amount related to the contingent consideration should Trawler recognize in Year 2 earnings?

choices.label: C
choices.text: No amount; the $700,000 cumulative excess over the acquisition-date fair value increases goodwill

questions.explanation: A liability-classified contingent consideration obligation is remeasured to fair value at each reporting date, with changes recognized in earnings. The $350,000 increase from $900,000 to $1,250,000 was already recognized in Year 1 earnings. In Year 2 only the further change to the $1,600,000 settlement amount is recognized, which is a $350,000 loss. The $700,000 amount is the cumulative change from the acquisition date and double counts the portion already recognized in Year 1. Adjusting goodwill is prohibited because these changes result from post-acquisition events rather than from new information about acquisition-date facts. The $1,600,000 amount treats the entire settlement payment as expense and ignores the liability already on the balance sheet.
questions.explanationJa: 負債に分類された条件付対価は各報告日に公正価値で再測定し、変動を損益に認識する。$900,000 から $1,250,000 への $350,000 の増加は Year 1 の損益で既に認識済み。Year 2 で認識するのは決済額 $1,600,000 までのさらなる変動のみであり、損失は $350,000 となる。$700,000 は取得日からの累積変動額で、Year 1 に認識済みの部分を二重計上している。のれんの修正は、これらの変動が取得日の事実に関する新情報ではなく取得日後の事象によるものであるため認められない。$1,600,000 は決済額全体を費用とし、既に計上されている負債を無視した誤り。

questions.subtopic: Measurement Period - Qualifying Adjustments
questions.stem: Which of the following events occurring after a business combination qualifies as a measurement period adjustment under ASC 805?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Six months after the acquisition date, a hurricane damages an acquired warehouse and reduces its fair value by $600,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Four months after the acquisition date, the acquirer's board approves a plan to close one of the acquiree's plants, and the acquirer estimates $600,000 of severance costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Three months after the acquisition date, the acquirer receives the completed appraisal of a building the acquiree owned at the acquisition date, showing an acquisition-date fair value $600,000 higher than the provisional amount recorded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nine months after the acquisition date, the acquirer increases the assumed warranty liability by $600,000 because of defects in units the acquiree sold after the acquisition date.

questions.explanation: A measurement period adjustment arises only from new information obtained about facts and circumstances that existed as of the acquisition date and that, if known, would have affected the measurement of amounts recognized at that date. A completed appraisal of an asset the acquiree already owned on the acquisition date supplies exactly that kind of information, so the $600,000 increase is recorded as an adjustment to the building and to goodwill. Hurricane damage occurring after the acquisition date is a post-acquisition event, and the loss is recognized in earnings. The acquirer's own plan to close a plant is a post-combination decision that does not create a liability assumed in the combination; the severance cost is expensed when the recognition criteria are met. Warranty claims arising from units sold after the acquisition date relate to post-acquisition transactions and are charged to earnings.
questions.explanationJa: 測定期間の修正は、取得日時点で存在していた事実・状況について新たに入手した情報に起因し、その情報を取得日に知っていれば認識額の測定に影響したであろう場合に限って生じる。被取得企業が取得日に既に保有していた資産の鑑定評価の完了はまさにその種の情報であり、$600,000 の増加は建物とのれんの修正として処理する。取得日後のハリケーンによる損傷は事後の事象であり、損失は当期損益に認識する。取得企業自身による工場閉鎖計画は結合後の意思決定であり、結合で引き受けた負債を生じさせないため、退職金は認識要件を満たした時点で費用処理する。取得日後に販売された製品から生じる保証請求は取得日後の取引に関するものであり損益に賦課する。

questions.subtopic: Measurement Period - Cumulative Catch-Up Adjustment
questions.stem: Marsden Corp, a calendar-year company, acquired Colby Inc on October 1, Year 1. Marsden provisionally recorded a customer relationship intangible asset at $4,000,000, amortized straight-line over 10 years with no residual value, and provisionally recorded goodwill of $2,500,000. Marsden issued its Year 1 financial statements in March Year 2. In May Year 2, and within the measurement period, Marsden received the final valuation showing that the acquisition-date fair value of the customer relationship intangible was $4,600,000. No other amounts changed. What should Marsden report?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Goodwill of $1,900,000, with the Year 1 financial statements retrospectively restated to increase amortization expense by $15,000

choices.label: B
choices.text: Goodwill of $2,500,000, with a $600,000 gain recognized in Year 2 earnings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Goodwill of $3,100,000, with $15,000 of additional amortization expense recognized in Year 2

choices.label: D
choices.text: Goodwill of $1,900,000, with $15,000 of additional amortization expense recognized in Year 2

questions.explanation: A measurement period adjustment that increases an acquired asset reduces goodwill by the same amount, so goodwill becomes $1,900,000 ($2,500,000 less $600,000). Since ASU 2015-16, the acquirer does not retrospectively restate prior period financial statements for measurement period adjustments. Instead, the adjustment is recognized in the reporting period in which it is determined, and the effect on earnings that would have been recorded in prior periods is recognized in the current period as a cumulative catch-up. Amortization for the three months from October 1 to December 31, Year 1 was $100,000 ($4,000,000 / 10 x 3/12) but should have been $115,000 ($4,600,000 / 10 x 3/12), so $15,000 of additional amortization is recognized in Year 2 along with normal Year 2 amortization. Restating Year 1 reflects the superseded requirement. Goodwill of $2,500,000 with a $600,000 gain treats the revision as income rather than as a reallocation of the purchase price. Goodwill of $3,100,000 increases goodwill for the higher intangible value instead of decreasing it.
questions.explanationJa: 取得資産を増額する測定期間の修正は、同額だけのれんを減少させるため、のれんは $2,500,000 − $600,000 = $1,900,000 となる。ASU 2015-16 以降、測定期間の修正について過年度の財務諸表を遡及的に修正再表示することはない。修正は確定した報告期間に認識し、過年度に計上されていたはずの損益影響は当期に累積キャッチアップとして認識する。Year 1 の10月1日から12月31日までの3か月の償却費は $4,000,000 ÷ 10 × 3/12 = $100,000 であったが、本来は $4,600,000 ÷ 10 × 3/12 = $115,000 であるため、差額 $15,000 を Year 2 の通常の償却費に加えて認識する。Year 1 の修正再表示は旧基準の要求。のれん $2,500,000 に $600,000 の利益を計上する処理は、取得対価の再配分ではなく収益として扱った誤り。のれん $3,100,000 は無形資産の増額分だけのれんを減らすべきところを増やした誤り。

questions.subtopic: Measurement Period - Revised Goodwill Calculation
questions.stem:
Ashland Corp acquired Vint Inc on June 1, Year 1 and provisionally recorded goodwill of $3,200,000. Before the measurement period closed, Ashland determined the following:
An appraisal of the machinery's condition on June 1, Year 1 showed the acquisition-date fair value of the acquired machinery was $700,000 higher than the provisional amount.
A site study showed that contamination existing on June 1, Year 1 made the acquisition-date fair value of the assumed environmental remediation liability $450,000 higher than the provisional amount.
A customer of Vint suffered a fire in August Year 1 and filed for bankruptcy in September Year 1, making a $300,000 acquired trade receivable uncollectible.
What is Ashland's revised goodwill?
questions.explanation: The machinery appraisal and the environmental site study both provide new information about conditions that existed on the acquisition date, so both are measurement period adjustments. Increasing an acquired asset by $700,000 decreases goodwill, and increasing an assumed liability by $450,000 increases goodwill, giving revised goodwill of $2,950,000 ($3,200,000 less $700,000 plus $450,000). The receivable became uncollectible because of a fire that occurred in August Year 1, after the acquisition date, so it is a post-acquisition credit loss charged to earnings rather than a goodwill adjustment. The $3,250,000 amount treats the uncollectible receivable as a measurement period adjustment. The $3,450,000 amount reverses the direction of both adjustments. The $2,500,000 amount records only the machinery adjustment and ignores the increase in the assumed remediation liability.
questions.explanationJa: 機械の鑑定と土壌調査はいずれも取得日に存在していた状況に関する新情報を提供するため、双方とも測定期間の修正に該当する。取得資産を $700,000 増額するとのれんは減少し、引き受けた負債を $450,000 増額するとのれんは増加するため、修正後ののれんは $3,200,000 − $700,000 + $450,000 = $2,950,000。売掛金が回収不能になったのは取得日後である Year 1 の8月の火災が原因なので、のれんの修正ではなく取得日後の貸倒損失として損益に賦課する。$3,250,000 は回収不能債権を測定期間の修正として扱った誤り。$3,450,000 は2つの修正の方向を逆にした誤り。$2,500,000 は機械の修正のみを反映し、引き受けた環境修復負債の増加を無視した金額。

questions.subtopic: Bargain Purchase With Previously Held Interest
questions.stem: Pinnacle Corp owned a 25% interest in Ryder Inc accounted for under the equity method, with a carrying amount of $1,900,000 on January 2, Year 4. On that date Pinnacle acquired Ryder's remaining 75% for $5,400,000 cash and obtained control. The acquisition-date fair value of the previously held 25% interest was $1,800,000, and the acquisition-date fair value of Ryder's identifiable net assets was $7,600,000. Pinnacle has reassessed its identification and measurement of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed and confirmed the amounts. What bargain purchase gain should Pinnacle recognize?

choices.label: D
choices.text: No gain; the excess is allocated as a pro rata reduction of the acquired nonfinancial assets

questions.explanation: In a business combination achieved in stages, the acquisition-date fair value of the previously held interest is added to the consideration transferred in the goodwill or bargain purchase computation. The total is $7,200,000 ($5,400,000 cash plus the $1,800,000 fair value of the previously held interest), which is $400,000 less than the $7,600,000 fair value of the identifiable net assets, so a $400,000 bargain purchase gain is recognized in earnings on the acquisition date. The $100,000 decline from the $1,900,000 carrying amount of the previously held interest to its $1,800,000 fair value is a separate remeasurement loss and does not reduce the bargain purchase gain. The $300,000 amount uses the $1,900,000 carrying amount instead of the required fair value. The $2,200,000 amount omits the previously held interest from the computation. Allocating the excess as a pro rata reduction of nonfinancial assets is the treatment required in an asset acquisition, not in a business combination.
questions.explanationJa: 段階取得による企業結合では、のれんまたは負ののれんの計算において従前保有持分の取得日公正価値を移転対価に加算する。合計は現金 $5,400,000 + 従前保有持分の公正価値 $1,800,000 = $7,200,000 で、識別可能純資産の公正価値 $7,600,000 を $400,000 下回るため、取得日に $400,000 の負ののれん利益を損益に認識する。従前保有持分の帳簿価額 $1,900,000 から公正価値 $1,800,000 への $100,000 の下落は別個の再測定損失であり、負ののれん利益を減額しない。$300,000 は公正価値ではなく帳簿価額 $1,900,000 を用いた誤り。$2,200,000 は従前保有持分を計算から除外した誤り。超過額を非金融資産の按分減額とする処理は、企業結合ではなく資産の取得に求められる処理である。

questions.subtopic: Bargain Purchase - Attribution Between Parent and NCI
questions.stem: Quorum Corp acquires 80% of Selby Inc for $3,600,000 cash. The acquisition-date fair value of the 20% noncontrolling interest is $880,000, and the acquisition-date fair value of Selby's identifiable net assets is $5,000,000. After completing the required reassessment, Quorum concludes that a bargain purchase has occurred and computes a $520,000 gain. How should the $520,000 gain be attributed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $416,000 is attributed to Quorum and $104,000 to the noncontrolling interest, in proportion to their ownership.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entire $520,000 is recorded as a reduction of the noncontrolling interest, lowering it to $360,000.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The entire $520,000 is attributed to Quorum, and the noncontrolling interest remains at $880,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The $520,000 is reported in other comprehensive income and attributed $416,000 to Quorum and $104,000 to the noncontrolling interest.

questions.explanation: The gain is $520,000 ($5,000,000 of identifiable net assets less the sum of the $3,600,000 consideration transferred and the $880,000 fair value of the noncontrolling interest). ASC 805-30-25-2 requires the acquirer to recognize the entire bargain purchase gain in earnings on the acquisition date and attribute it to the acquirer, because the bargain arises from the terms the acquirer negotiated rather than from the noncontrolling shareholders' position. The noncontrolling interest continues to be reported at its $880,000 acquisition-date fair value. Splitting the gain 80/20 applies the income attribution rule used for post-acquisition subsidiary earnings, which does not govern the acquisition-date gain. Reducing the noncontrolling interest to $360,000 would abandon the required fair value measurement of the noncontrolling interest. The gain is reported in earnings, not in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanationJa: 利得は識別可能純資産 $5,000,000 −（移転対価 $3,600,000 + 非支配持分の公正価値 $880,000）= $520,000。ASC 805-30-25-2 は、負ののれん利益の全額を取得日に損益で認識し、取得企業に帰属させることを求める。有利な条件は取得企業が交渉した取引条件から生じるものであり、非支配株主の立場から生じるものではないためである。非支配持分は取得日公正価値 $880,000 のまま計上を続ける。80対20で按分する処理は取得日後の子会社利益の帰属ルールを当てはめたもので、取得日の利得には適用されない。非支配持分を $360,000 まで減額する処理は、非支配持分の公正価値測定という要求事項を放棄することになる。利得はその他の包括利益ではなく当期損益に計上する。

questions.subtopic: Identifiable Net Assets Acquired
questions.stem:
Beacon Corp acquires 100% of Tilden Inc. On the acquisition date, Tilden's balance sheet reports net assets with a book value of $6,200,000, which includes $900,000 of goodwill recognized in Tilden's own earlier acquisition of another company. Beacon's valuation identifies the following:
Tilden's inventory is undervalued by $350,000
Tilden's land is undervalued by $1,100,000
An unrecorded trade name has a fair value of $800,000
Tilden's assembled workforce has an estimated fair value of $600,000
An unrecorded lawsuit against Tilden arising from a contractual dispute has an acquisition-date fair value of $250,000
All other carrying amounts approximate fair value. What is the acquisition-date fair value of Tilden's identifiable net assets?
questions.explanation: Start with the $6,200,000 book value and remove Tilden's own $900,000 of goodwill, because goodwill previously recognized by the acquiree is not an identifiable asset and is never carried forward. Add the $350,000 inventory step-up, the $1,100,000 land step-up, and the $800,000 trade name, which is identifiable because it arises from legal rights and is separable. Deduct the $250,000 lawsuit, which is a contractual contingency measured at acquisition-date fair value. The result is $7,300,000. The assembled workforce is explicitly excluded from separate recognition under ASC 805-20-55-6 and is subsumed into goodwill, so the $7,900,000 amount improperly recognizes it. The $8,200,000 amount leaves Tilden's own goodwill in identifiable net assets. The $7,550,000 amount omits the assumed lawsuit liability.
questions.explanationJa: 帳簿価額 $6,200,000 から出発し、Tilden 自身の過去の取得で計上したのれん $900,000 を除外する。被取得企業が既に計上していたのれんは識別可能資産ではなく引き継がれないためである。棚卸資産の評価差額 $350,000、土地の評価差額 $1,100,000、および法的権利から生じ分離可能であるため識別可能である商標名 $800,000 を加算する。契約から生じる偶発事象として取得日公正価値で測定される訴訟 $250,000 を控除する。結果は $7,300,000。組織化された労働力は ASC 805-20-55-6 により個別認識が明示的に否定され、のれんに含められるため、$7,900,000 はこれを誤って計上した金額。$8,200,000 は Tilden 自身ののれんを識別可能純資産に残したままの金額。$7,550,000 は引き受けた訴訟負債を漏らした金額。

questions.subtopic: NCI Measured at Fair Value - Control Premium
questions.stem: Ellery Corp acquires 90,000 of Fenwick Inc's 120,000 outstanding common shares for $48 per share in cash and obtains control. Fenwick's shares trade on an active market at $42 per share both immediately before and immediately after the acquisition; the $6 per share difference reflects the control premium Ellery paid. The acquisition-date fair value of Fenwick's identifiable net assets is $4,900,000. Ellery elects to measure the noncontrolling interest at fair value. What amount of goodwill should Ellery recognize?
questions.explanation: Consideration transferred is $4,320,000 (90,000 shares x $48). When an active market price is available for the shares not held by the acquirer, ASC 805-20-30-7 states that the quoted price of those shares is generally the best evidence of the fair value of the noncontrolling interest, and the per share fair value of the noncontrolling interest may differ from the per share amount the acquirer pays because of the control premium. The noncontrolling interest is therefore $1,260,000 (30,000 shares x $42). Goodwill is $680,000 ($4,320,000 plus $1,260,000 less the $4,900,000 of identifiable net assets). The $645,000 amount measures the noncontrolling interest at its proportionate 25% share of identifiable net assets rather than at fair value as elected. The $860,000 amount grosses the noncontrolling interest up at the $48 control price, ignoring that the control premium does not attach to the shares the acquirer did not buy. The $1,905,000 amount recognizes only the acquirer's 75% share of the identifiable net assets while including 100% of the noncontrolling interest fair value.
questions.explanationJa: 移転対価は 90,000 株 × $48 = $4,320,000。取得企業が保有しない株式に活発な市場価格がある場合、ASC 805-20-30-7 はその市場価格が非支配持分の公正価値の最善の証拠であるのが通常であり、支配プレミアムのために非支配持分の1株当たり公正価値が取得企業の支払額と異なり得ると述べている。したがって非支配持分は 30,000 株 × $42 = $1,260,000。のれんは $4,320,000 + $1,260,000 − 識別可能純資産 $4,900,000 = $680,000。$645,000 は非支配持分を選択した公正価値ではなく識別可能純資産の25%相当額で測定した金額。$860,000 は非支配持分を支配価格 $48 で引き直したもので、取得企業が買わなかった株式には支配プレミアムが付かない点を無視している。$1,905,000 は識別可能純資産を取得企業の75%分しか計上せず、非支配持分は全額含めた不整合な金額。

questions.subtopic: Acquisition-Date Recording - Separate vs Consolidated Statements
questions.stem: On the acquisition date, Harlow Corp pays $9,000,000 cash for 100% of the outstanding common stock of Ives Inc. Ives continues to exist as a separate legal entity and prepares its own separate financial statements. Ives does not elect push-down accounting. Which statement correctly describes the accounting on the acquisition date?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Harlow records Ives's identifiable assets and liabilities at their acquisition-date fair values, plus goodwill, directly in Harlow's own separate financial statements.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Harlow records a $9,000,000 investment in its separate financial statements; Ives's identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value and the resulting goodwill appear only in the consolidated financial statements, where the investment account is eliminated against Ives's equity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Harlow records the investment at Harlow's share of the book value of Ives's net assets, and the difference between that amount and the cash paid is reported as a deferred charge.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ives is required to remeasure its own assets and liabilities to their acquisition-date fair values in its separate financial statements.

questions.explanation: Because Ives survives as a separate legal entity, Harlow's separate books carry an investment account measured at the $9,000,000 fair value of the consideration transferred. The acquisition method is applied in the consolidation working papers: Ives's identifiable assets and liabilities are stated at acquisition-date fair value, goodwill is recognized for the excess of consideration over those net assets, and the investment account is eliminated against Ives's pre-acquisition equity so that none of Ives's pre-acquisition retained earnings carries into consolidated retained earnings. Recording the fair values and goodwill directly on Harlow's books describes a statutory merger in which the acquiree is dissolved, which is not the case here. Measuring the investment at the acquiree's book value with a deferred charge is not permitted under any method. Push-down accounting, which would let Ives remeasure its own assets in its separate statements, is an election available to the acquiree and is not required.
questions.explanationJa: Ives が別法人として存続するため、Harlow の個別財務諸表には移転対価の公正価値 $9,000,000 で測定された投資勘定が計上される。取得法は連結精算表上で適用され、Ives の識別可能資産・負債を取得日公正価値で表示し、対価が当該純資産を上回る額をのれんとして認識し、投資勘定を Ives の取得前資本と相殺消去する。これにより Ives の取得前利益剰余金は連結利益剰余金に引き継がれない。公正価値とのれんを Harlow の帳簿に直接計上するのは被取得企業が消滅する吸収合併の説明であり、本件には当てはまらない。投資を被取得企業の帳簿価額で測定し差額を繰延費用とする処理はいずれの方法でも認められない。Ives が個別財務諸表で自らの資産を再測定するプッシュダウン会計は被取得企業に認められた選択であって強制ではない。

questions.subtopic: Consolidated Stockholders' Equity at Acquisition
questions.stem: Immediately before acquiring Brandt Inc on January 2, Year 5, Calder Corp reported stockholders' equity of common stock $2,000,000, additional paid-in capital $5,000,000, and retained earnings $9,000,000. On that date Calder acquired 70% of Brandt by paying $3,000,000 cash and issuing shares with a fair value of $4,500,000 and a par value of $500,000. The acquisition-date fair value of the 30% noncontrolling interest was $3,200,000. Brandt's stockholders' equity consisted of common stock $1,000,000 and retained earnings $5,000,000, and the acquisition-date fair value of Brandt's identifiable net assets was $8,000,000. Calder also paid $250,000 of legal and advisory fees related to the acquisition. What is consolidated total stockholders' equity immediately after the acquisition?
questions.explanation: Consolidated equity attributable to the parent starts with Calder's $16,000,000 of equity, increases by the $4,500,000 fair value of the shares issued as consideration, and decreases by the $250,000 of acquisition-related costs that must be expensed, giving $20,250,000. The noncontrolling interest of $3,200,000 is reported within consolidated stockholders' equity under ASC 810-10-45-15, so consolidated total stockholders' equity is $23,450,000. Brandt's $6,000,000 of pre-acquisition equity is eliminated in full against the investment account and the noncontrolling interest, so none of it survives. The $20,250,000 amount omits the noncontrolling interest, which would improperly present it outside equity. The $23,700,000 amount fails to expense the $250,000 of acquisition-related costs. The $26,250,000 amount adds Brandt's pre-acquisition equity instead of eliminating it and omits the noncontrolling interest.
questions.explanationJa: 親会社持分は Calder の資本 $16,000,000 から出発し、対価として発行した株式の公正価値 $4,500,000 を加算し、費用処理が必要な取得関連費用 $250,000 を減算して $20,250,000。非支配持分 $3,200,000 は ASC 810-10-45-15 により連結上の株主資本の内部に表示されるため、連結株主資本合計は $23,450,000 となる。Brandt の取得前資本 $6,000,000 は投資勘定と非支配持分に対して全額消去され、残らない。$20,250,000 は非支配持分を含めておらず、資本の外に表示することになる誤り。$23,700,000 は取得関連費用 $250,000 を費用処理していない金額。$26,250,000 は Brandt の取得前資本を消去せず加算し、非支配持分を含めていない金額。

questions.subtopic: Consolidated Retained Earnings at Acquisition
questions.stem: On July 1, Year 2, Dunmore Corp acquired 100% of Everly Inc. Immediately before the acquisition, Dunmore's retained earnings were $14,600,000 and Everly's retained earnings were $3,800,000. Dunmore paid $9,000,000 cash and issued its own shares with a fair value of $2,000,000. In connection with the transaction, Dunmore incurred $350,000 of due diligence and legal fees and $120,000 of costs to register the shares issued. What amount of consolidated retained earnings should Dunmore report immediately after the acquisition?
questions.explanation: Consolidated retained earnings immediately after an acquisition equal the parent's retained earnings; the acquiree's pre-acquisition retained earnings are eliminated against the investment account and never carry into consolidated retained earnings. The $350,000 of due diligence and legal fees are acquisition-related costs expensed as incurred, which reduces Dunmore's retained earnings to $14,250,000. The $120,000 of share registration costs are charged against additional paid-in capital rather than earnings, so they do not affect retained earnings. The $14,600,000 amount ignores the required expensing of the acquisition-related costs. The $18,050,000 amount improperly adds Everly's $3,800,000 of pre-acquisition retained earnings. The $14,130,000 amount also deducts the share registration costs from retained earnings instead of charging them to additional paid-in capital.
questions.explanationJa: 取得直後の連結利益剰余金は親会社の利益剰余金に等しい。被取得企業の取得前利益剰余金は投資勘定と相殺消去され、連結利益剰余金に引き継がれることはない。デューデリジェンス・法務費用 $350,000 は発生時に費用処理する取得関連費用であり、Dunmore の利益剰余金は $14,250,000 に減少する。株式の登録費用 $120,000 は損益ではなく資本剰余金に賦課されるため、利益剰余金に影響しない。$14,600,000 は取得関連費用の費用処理を無視した金額。$18,050,000 は Everly の取得前利益剰余金 $3,800,000 を誤って加算した金額。$14,130,000 は株式登録費用を資本剰余金ではなく利益剰余金から控除した誤り。

questions.subtopic: VIE - Sufficiency of Equity Investment at Risk
questions.stem: Ridgeline Corp sponsored the formation of Crest LLC to build and operate a distribution center. Crest's total assets are $50,000,000, funded by $46,000,000 of nonrecourse debt that Ridgeline guarantees and $4,000,000 of equity. Of the equity, $2,800,000 was contributed by an unrelated investor from its own funds, and $1,200,000 was contributed by a second investor that borrowed the entire amount from Ridgeline on a nonrecourse basis. Crest's expected losses are estimated at $5,500,000. Which conclusion is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Crest's equity investment at risk is $2,800,000, which is not sufficient to absorb its $5,500,000 of expected losses, so Crest is a variable interest entity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crest's equity investment at risk is $4,000,000, which is 8% of total assets and therefore sufficient, so Crest is not a variable interest entity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Crest's equity investment at risk is $2,800,000, but because Ridgeline's guarantee of the nonrecourse debt is not a variable interest, Crest is not a variable interest entity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crest is not a variable interest entity because a single unrelated investor holds a majority of the equity and therefore directs Crest's activities.

questions.explanation: ASC 810-10-15-14 excludes from the equity investment at risk any equity interests that were funded directly or indirectly by the reporting entity or its related parties, so the $1,200,000 contributed with money borrowed from Ridgeline does not count. Equity at risk is therefore $2,800,000, which is below the $5,500,000 of expected losses, and the entity is a variable interest entity on that basis. The 10% of total assets benchmark is only a presumption that can be overcome by an expected loss analysis; it is not a safe harbor, and the equity here falls short of the expected losses regardless. Ridgeline's guarantee of the nonrecourse debt is a variable interest because it absorbs variability that would otherwise be borne by Crest's other interest holders, and it reinforces rather than defeats the VIE conclusion. The size of an investor's equity stake does not determine VIE status when the equity at risk is insufficient, because the analysis then moves to the primary beneficiary model rather than the voting interest model.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 810-10-15-14 は、報告企業またはその関連当事者が直接的・間接的に資金提供した持分をリスクに晒された出資から除外するため、Ridgeline からの借入金で拠出された $1,200,000 は算入されない。したがってリスクに晒された出資は $2,800,000 であり、予想損失 $5,500,000 を下回るため、この点から変動持分事業体に該当する。総資産の10%という目安は予想損失の分析によって覆し得る推定にすぎずセーフハーバーではなく、いずれにせよ本件の出資は予想損失に届かない。Ridgeline によるノンリコース債務の保証は、他の持分保有者が本来負担するはずの変動性を吸収するため変動持分に該当し、VIE という結論を否定するどころか補強する。リスクに晒された出資が不十分な場合、分析は議決権モデルではなく主たる受益者の判定へ移るため、出資者の持分比率の大小だけで VIE 該当性は決まらない。

questions.subtopic: VIE - Primary Beneficiary Determination
questions.stem: Tessell Corp and Vance Corp are unrelated parties that each hold a variable interest in Wexler LLC, which has been determined to be a variable interest entity. Tessell has the unilateral power to direct Wexler's construction and leasing activities, which are the activities that most significantly affect Wexler's economic performance, and Tessell holds an interest that exposes it to approximately 30% of Wexler's expected losses and expected residual returns. Vance holds a subordinated note and a residual value guarantee that expose it to approximately 55% of Wexler's expected losses and expected residual returns, but Vance has no decision-making rights and no kick-out rights over Tessell. Which party must consolidate Wexler?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vance, because it absorbs the majority of Wexler's expected losses and expected residual returns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tessell, because it has the power to direct the activities that most significantly affect Wexler's economic performance and holds an interest that could potentially be significant to Wexler.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither; because power and the majority of the economic exposure are held by different parties, no party is the primary beneficiary and each accounts for its interest at fair value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both; Tessell consolidates Wexler's operating activities and Vance consolidates Wexler's financing activities under the silo provisions.

questions.explanation: The primary beneficiary is the single party that has both the power to direct the activities that most significantly affect the VIE's economic performance and the obligation to absorb losses or the right to receive benefits that could potentially be significant to the VIE. Both conditions are satisfied only by Tessell, which holds the unilateral power and an exposure of roughly 30% that is clearly more than insignificant, so Tessell consolidates Wexler. Absorbing a majority of the expected losses does not make Vance the primary beneficiary, because the current model does not use a majority-of-losses test and Vance lacks power. Concluding that no party consolidates ignores that Tessell meets both conditions. Silo accounting applies only when specified assets of a VIE are essentially the only source of payment for specified liabilities, which is not described here, and it never results in two parties consolidating the same entity.
questions.explanationJa: 主たる受益者とは、VIE の経済的パフォーマンスに最も重要な影響を与える活動を指図する力と、当該 VIE にとって重要となり得る損失の負担義務または便益の享受権の双方を有する単一の当事者である。双方の要件を満たすのは、一方的な指図権と明らかに軽微とはいえない約30%のエクスポージャーを持つ Tessell だけであり、Tessell が Wexler を連結する。予想損失の過半を吸収していても Vance は主たる受益者にはならない。現行モデルは損失の過半という基準を用いておらず、Vance には指図権がないためである。いずれも連結しないという結論は、Tessell が両要件を満たしている点を見落としている。サイロの規定は VIE の特定の資産が特定の負債の実質的に唯一の弁済原資である場合にのみ適用され、本件には当てはまらず、2者が同一の事業体を連結する結果を生むこともない。

questions.subtopic: VIE - Initial Consolidation of a VIE That Is Not a Business
questions.stem: Northgate Corp pays $2,000,000 cash for an interest in Quarry LLC and on that date becomes the primary beneficiary of Quarry, which is a variable interest entity that holds a portfolio of royalty contracts and does not meet the definition of a business. Northgate held no interest in Quarry before this transaction, and Quarry is not under common control with Northgate. On that date the fair value of Quarry's assets is $18,000,000, the fair value of its liabilities is $15,500,000, and the fair value of the noncontrolling interests in Quarry is $1,000,000. What should Northgate recognize on initial consolidation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $500,000 of goodwill

choices.label: B
choices.text: No gain, loss, or goodwill; Quarry's assets and liabilities are recorded at the carrying amounts in Quarry's own books

choices.label: C
choices.text: A $500,000 loss in earnings, and no goodwill

choices.label: D
choices.text: A $500,000 loss in other comprehensive income, and no goodwill

questions.explanation: When a reporting entity becomes the primary beneficiary of a VIE that is not a business, ASC 810-10-30-4 prohibits recognizing goodwill. The assets and liabilities are measured at fair value, and the difference between the sum of the consideration paid, the fair value of the noncontrolling interests, and the reported amount of any previously held interests, and the net amount of the identifiable assets and liabilities, is recognized as a gain or loss in earnings. Here that sum is $3,000,000 ($2,000,000 consideration plus $1,000,000 of noncontrolling interests) against net identifiable assets of $2,500,000 ($18,000,000 less $15,500,000), producing a $500,000 loss. Recognizing $500,000 of goodwill would be correct only if Quarry met the definition of a business. Recording the assets and liabilities at Quarry's carrying amounts applies the treatment required only when the VIE is under common control with the primary beneficiary. The difference is recognized in earnings, not in other comprehensive income.
questions.explanationJa: 報告企業が事業に該当しない VIE の主たる受益者となった場合、ASC 810-10-30-4 はのれんの認識を禁じている。資産・負債は公正価値で測定し、支払対価・非支配持分の公正価値・従前保有持分の計上額の合計と、識別可能資産・負債の純額との差額を損益に認識する。本件では合計が対価 $2,000,000 + 非支配持分 $1,000,000 = $3,000,000、識別可能純資産が $18,000,000 − $15,500,000 = $2,500,000 であり、差額 $500,000 の損失となる。$500,000 をのれんとする処理は Quarry が事業の定義を満たす場合にのみ正しい。資産・負債を Quarry の帳簿価額で計上する処理は、VIE が主たる受益者と共通支配下にある場合にのみ求められる処理である。差額はその他の包括利益ではなく当期損益に認識する。

questions.subtopic: VIE - Maximum Exposure to Loss Disclosure
questions.stem: Sentinel Corp holds variable interests in Dune LLC, a variable interest entity that Sentinel does not consolidate because it is not the primary beneficiary. Sentinel's involvement with Dune consists of an equity investment with a carrying amount of $2,400,000, a loan receivable from Dune with a carrying amount of $3,100,000, an unfunded commitment to lend Dune an additional $1,500,000, and a guarantee of $2,000,000 of Dune's third-party debt for which Sentinel has recorded a $250,000 guarantee liability. Dune's total assets are $40,000,000. What amount should Sentinel disclose as its maximum exposure to loss from its involvement with Dune?
questions.explanation: ASC 810-10-50-4 requires a reporting entity with a variable interest in an unconsolidated VIE to disclose its maximum exposure to loss, determined without regard to the probability of loss and without offsetting by any expected recoveries. The disclosure includes the $2,400,000 carrying amount of the equity investment, the $3,100,000 carrying amount of the loan receivable, the full $1,500,000 unfunded lending commitment, and the full $2,000,000 notional amount of the guarantee, for a total of $9,000,000. The $7,250,000 amount uses the $250,000 recorded guarantee liability instead of the $2,000,000 the guarantee could require Sentinel to pay. The $5,500,000 amount includes only the recognized assets and ignores the off-balance-sheet commitment and guarantee. The $40,000,000 amount is the VIE's total assets, which measures the size of the entity rather than Sentinel's exposure.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 810-10-50-4 は、連結しない VIE に変動持分を有する報告企業に対し、損失発生の確率を考慮せず、予想回収額と相殺もせずに、最大損失エクスポージャーを開示することを求めている。開示には、出資の帳簿価額 $2,400,000、貸付金の帳簿価額 $3,100,000、未実行の融資コミットメント全額 $1,500,000、保証の想定元本全額 $2,000,000 が含まれ、合計 $9,000,000 となる。$7,250,000 は Sentinel が支払を求められ得る $2,000,000 ではなく、計上済みの保証債務 $250,000 を用いた誤り。$5,500,000 は計上済み資産のみを含め、オフバランスのコミットメントと保証を無視した金額。$40,000,000 は VIE の総資産であり、事業体の規模を示すもので Sentinel のエクスポージャーではない。

questions.subtopic: VIE - Presentation by the Primary Beneficiary
questions.stem: Meridian Corp has concluded that it is the primary beneficiary of Harbor Point LLC, a variable interest entity, and consolidates it. Which of the following is required in Meridian's consolidated financial statements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Present separately on the face of the consolidated balance sheet, or parenthetically, the assets of the VIE that can be used only to settle the VIE's obligations and the liabilities of the VIE for which creditors have no recourse to the general credit of the primary beneficiary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Report Meridian's interest in the VIE as a single-line equity method investment and disclose the VIE's summarized financial data in the notes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Present the VIE's results of operations as a discontinued operation until Meridian deconsolidates the VIE.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Record the VIE's assets and liabilities at Meridian's historical cost and disclose their fair values only in the notes.

questions.explanation: ASC 810-10-45-25 requires the primary beneficiary to present separately, on the face of the consolidated balance sheet or parenthetically, the VIE's assets that can be used only to settle the VIE's obligations and the VIE's liabilities for which creditors or beneficial interest holders have no recourse to the general credit of the primary beneficiary. This presentation tells users which consolidated assets are not available to the primary beneficiary's own creditors and which consolidated liabilities do not expose it to loss. Reporting a single-line equity method investment would defeat consolidation, which requires the VIE's individual assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses to be combined line by line with those of the primary beneficiary. Discontinued operations presentation applies only to a component that has been disposed of or is held for sale and meets a strategic shift threshold. Initial measurement is at fair value when the VIE is not under common control, not at the primary beneficiary's historical cost.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 810-10-45-25 は主たる受益者に対し、VIE の債務の決済にのみ充当できる VIE の資産と、債権者または受益権保有者が主たる受益者の一般信用に遡求できない VIE の負債とを、連結貸借対照表の本体または括弧書きで区分表示することを求めている。この表示により、連結された資産のうち主たる受益者自身の債権者が引き当てにできないものと、連結された負債のうち主たる受益者に損失リスクを及ぼさないものが利用者に示される。持分法による一行表示は連結を否定するものであり、連結では VIE の個々の資産・負債・収益・費用を主たる受益者のものと項目ごとに合算する必要がある。非継続事業としての表示は、処分済みまたは売却目的保有で戦略的転換の要件を満たす構成単位にのみ適用される。共通支配下にない VIE の当初測定は主たる受益者の取得原価ではなく公正価値による。
